value.answer: Sorry you're dealing with that. If it gets urgent, ConnexOntario answers 24 hours a day at 1-866-531-2600, and Distress Centres of Greater Toronto has free 24/7 support by phone, chat or text. For regular therapy in Toronto: public care through a hospital or family clinic is usually covered by OHIP, but it often needs a doctor's referral and can mean a long wait. Private therapy isn't covered by OHIP, though many employer extended health plans cover it, and your workplace EAP may include a few free sessions a year. Cheaper options: Ontario Structured Psychotherapy gives free short-term CBT for adults with depression or anxiety, Family Service Toronto charges sliding-scale fees based on income, and the U of T and TMU training clinics offer reduced rates. For a private therapist, Psychotherapy Referral Service is a not-for-profit that can connect you with registered psychotherapists, and First Session offers free consultations. I couldn't get a phone number for the Distress Centres, so check their site for that.
